title: ID0429525-DC/Si-D/NZ-[MP / N5 160345946] Charging issue
description:
Reported issue:
Several charging sessions have started normally but the bus drivers
are reporting after about 40 minutes the power delivery from the
charger drops dramatically. The is means the buses are not
charging up overnight. Here are some session dates . Note the
times are UTC + 12
• from 6:20pm on 04 June to 4:00am on 05 June
• from 6:20pm on 03 June to 4:00am on 04 June
• 31 May, not sure the exact times but around midday to 3:00pm
Solution: converter replacement

additional_info.subject: RE: ID0429525-DC/Si-D/NZ-[MP / N5 160345946] Charging issue CRM:02678000083
additional_info.body:
Hello Liz,
We have heard back from the global technical team on this topic.
It appears that one of the power modules is having issues within the charger and would require attention.
Site work to inspect connectors of affected power module [serial number:
2102312VGQ10L6000024]
.
Ensure they are not damaged and correctly connected. Following that there might be two options:
1) Identify the position of the above mentioned serial number in the charge. Replace the affected power module with a new one.
1x 8EM5903-0AA01-0AA2. You can also use 1x 8EM5905-0AA00-2AA8, however this is the upgrade kit and thus there will be cabling that will be unused.
2) The charger is currently a 300kW configuration, meaning it has all the power modules populated (15 in total).
You could check with the customer if they require the full 300kW and if not reduce the maximum output capacity by removing the affected power module. The AC and DC power cables would also need to be removed from the charger for this module and we would need to reconfigure the charger for the current number of modules.
We will need to know from which group the module was removed (based on where the DC+ and DC- connections are made within the charger).
Estimated 2 hours of support from our side; which includes reconfiguration, confirmation and remote validation from onsite charging test.
I have included our schedule of rates for your review, the estimation would include the Order Handling Charge + Estimated 2 hours of Subject Matter Expert (eMobility).
Normally, there is a minimum of 4 hours per each job, but in this case we will good will that for the above mentioned 2 hours.
Providing your required details on the Schedule of rates and a Purchare Order, will allow us to start booking in the work.
Thanks and looking forward to hearing from you,
With Kind Regards,
Ferdinand Reisch
Siemens Ltd.
Application Service Engineer
Email: ferdinand.reisch@siemens.com
www.siemens.com.au/emobility

additional_info.subject: RE: ID0429525-DC/Si-D/NZ-[MP / N5 160345946] Charging issue CRM:02678000083
additional_info.body:
Hello Liz,
The charger will be de-rated to 280kW, by removing 1 power module.
If there is the intention to set it back to 300kW, the standard power upgrade kit would need to be installed (power module, wiring and charger configuration).
This statement of course only holds true, so long as the electrical installation is designed and installed to supply the charger with this intended power level.
We would suggest the SiCharge D technician intended to work on this task, review their applicable training material or repair manual (Repair manual section 2.2 Power Upgrade High Flex).
We must still maintain the correct power module placement within the charger (for 280kW), ensuring the correct TB numbering among the power matrix.
This may require moving another converter from within the charger in place of the defective one, if it is required and to be maintained for the 280kW.
You will only know which power module position it is, when it is physically matched with the serial number (from below) once on site.
With Kind Regards,
Ferdinand Reisch
Siemens Ltd.
Application Service Engineer
Email: ferdinand.reisch@siemens.com
www.siemens.com.au/emobility
